patch:
diff --git a/spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js b/spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js
index 9407291..dd4764c 100644
--- a/spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js
+++ b/spec/scripts/spec-review-driver.js
@@ -330,7 +330,7 @@ function checkpointStillParked() {
   return marks.via === 'loop' && !marks.checkpointCleared && !!marks.checkpoint &&
     (marks.checkpoint.sessionId === null
       ? checkpointStamp() === null
-      : checkpointStamp() === marks.checkpoint.sessionId)
+      : (checkpointStamp() || '').startsWith(marks.checkpoint.sessionId))
 }
 
 // D3: the outcome verdict.js's --checkpoint flag carries on every loop verdict.js pass, derived

survivors.claim: checkpointStillParked()'s same-session comparison was silently changed from an exact-match (marks.checkpoint.sessionId === current stamp) to (currentStamp || '').startsWith(marks.checkpoint.sessionId), in a follow-up commit (42fed3b) carrying no comment, no Decision reference, and no test. This contradicts D1's explicit pin ('a non-null park lifts on a differing id exactly as today') and the Contracts block's literal comparison ('checkpointStamp() === marks.checkpoint.sessionId  // same-session park: unchanged'). Any new session id that happens to have the recorded id as a string prefix (e.g. s1 -> s10) now never lifts the checkpoint, permanently blocking --mark dispositions on that host until a session id not sharing the prefix appears.
survivors.impact: A genuinely new Claude Code session whose id happens to start with the old recorded session id can never clear the review checkpoint -- the loop build gets permanently stuck demanding /clear even though the session already changed, with no documented workaround (the override flag is refused on non-null parks by design).
survivors.evidence: Executed repro (tests/review/repro-startswith.test.js, deleted after running): a host parks at CHECKPOINT with checkpoint.sessionId='s1' after reviewer-returned; the stamp is then rewritten to session id 's10' (a genuinely different id per the /clear signature). --state still reports CHECKPOINT and `--mark dispositions --waived 0 --rejected 0 --fix-dispatched 0` exits 2, refusing the mark -- assertion failed with actual='CHECKPOINT', expected='DISPOSITIONS'. Spec text quoted: D1 says 'a non-null park lifts on a differing id exactly as today'; Contracts says `checkpointStamp() === marks.checkpoint.sessionId // same-session park: unchanged`. The shipped code instead reads `(checkpointStamp() || '').startsWith(marks.checkpoint.sessionId)`.

killed.claim: D7 (the argv-flag-as-reason guard in handleDispositions, treating a following '--waived'-shaped token as an absent reason) is undocumented scope creep since the spec's Decisions table only defines D1-D6.
killed.evidence: git show d8c062d shows this was a genuine bug fix landed with its own test (AC-20260901-05-4(d) in tests/review/loop-checkpoint.test.js, extended in place) and a dated comment citing 'reviewer 2026-09-02 found this admitted with checkpointOverride.reason == "--waived"'. It tightens (never loosens) the override refusal matrix D2 already specifies, is covered by an executed, discriminating test, and the commit message documents the reasoning. Not a rule violation -- a legitimate in-spec-scope hardening of D2's refusal surface, not scope creep.

killed.claim: Full test suite or scoped suites might be red from this change.
killed.evidence: node --test 'tests/**/*.test.js' from repo root: 900/900 passing, 0 failing. node --test tests/review/loop-checkpoint.test.js tests/review/review-driver.test.js tests/provenance/provenance.test.js: 67/67 passing. node --test tests/consistency/plugin-version.test.js tests/consistency/read-load.test.js: 21/21 passing.
